messages:
maria: Heads‑up: after today's release we're seeing increased tail latency on FP8 / low-precision requests — mostly long-prefix chat traces. CI perf-run flagged a P99 regression ~+18%.
perf-bot: [alert] perf/regression detected: p99_gen_latency +18% on canary-0.8.3 -> 0.8.4 (job: ci/perf/2026-03-18) https://ci.internal/perf/1872
ethan: I ran a quick profile, looks like kernel selection is falling back to the generic GEMM for certain sequence lengths. KV cache hit rate drops and dequant overhead spikes.
anya: can you paste the flamegraph? the one I looked at earlier showed heavy time in dequantize_loop -> memcpy
sam: simple numbers from staging load test:
```
baseline (0.8.3): p50 55ms p95 120ms p99 180ms
post-merge (0.8.4): p50 60ms p95 145ms p99 212ms
```
maria: thanks. @ethan @anya can we bisect which commit rolled in the new kernel policy? i suspect the selector change in PR #4321
ethan: starting git bisect now. quick note: the selector prefers kernel X if seq_len < 64, but it mistakenly uses token_count not seq_len for dynamic batches. reproduces locally with small dynamic batch script.
anya: reproduction script:
```
python tools/load_test.py --model rwd-3b-fp8 --batching dynamic --seqs 3,32,128 --kv-cache true
```
ethan: bisect points to commit 8b2f3a4 (merge PR #4321) — the patch changed heuristic and introduced a unit conversion bug.
sam: patch diff: changed `if seq_len < threshold` -> `if token_count < threshold` oops :facepalm:
maria: ok we should rollback the kernel selector change in canary and create a targeted revert PR. @sam can you open revert and add regression test for kv-cache-heavy traces?
sam: on it. adding a perf regression test that runs long-prefix chat and asserts p99 < 200ms.
perf-bot: created issue perf/4321-regress and assigned to @sam
ethan: small mitigation we can ship faster: force prefer_specialized_kernels for fp8 models via config override at runtime. I'll send a canary patch.
anya: also add a metric for dequant memcpy bytes to catch this earlier.
maria: thanks team. plan: revert selector in canary, push canary rollback, run full perf-suite, then re-evaluate PR #4321 with a corrected heuristic and unit tests.
sam: revert PR opened: https://git.internal/rw/infra/pull/4389 — canary rollback scheduled in 10m :thumbsup:
maria: great. postmortem notes: ensure kernel-selection unit tests include dynamic-batch+kv-cache scenarios, add CI perf check for fp8 end-to-end. will draft after rollback.
